problem: Founder Yvon Chouinard did not want to sell or go public and wanted the company's profits to serve environmental goals.
title: Patagonia's founder transfers ownership to a trust and a climate nonprofit
context: Patagonia was a privately held company valued at about $3 billion.
decision_made: Give all voting stock (2 percent) to the Patagonia Purpose Trust and all non-voting stock (98 percent) to the Holdfast Collective, a climate nonprofit.
action_taken: Announced in September 2022; the company stays for-profit with unchanged leadership, and profits after reinvestment go to climate causes, estimated around $100 million a year.
observed_outcome: Not documented in the sources used.
lessons: Ownership structure can lock in a company's mission, trading off the option of selling or going public.
limitations: Only the announcement and structure were checked. The $100 million figure is an estimate. The Holdfast Collective is a 501(c)(4), which allows political activity but gives no income tax deduction.

claims.claim_text: Patagonia's voting stock went to a purpose trust and its non-voting stock to the Holdfast Collective.
Chouinard estimated the arrangement could direct about $100 million a year to climate causes.
